title: UPDATE: Iran Used AI for US Naval Targeting in OpenAI's Most Serious Ops
summary:
Two of the largest AI laboratories in the US have banned accounts used by foreign states to plant fake news and identify military vulnerabilities. Iranian actors leveraged models from OpenAI and Anthropic to develop targeting recommendations for attacks against US naval forces, according to separate investigations by the firms. These Iranian operatives also deployed seven fake Western journalist personas to place nearly 100 articles critical of the US war against Iran in a dozen or more outlets globally, which they then amplified with AI-generated social media comments.

OpenAI also disrupted a Russian influence operation it designated as its first "Category 5" and most complex front in 2.5 years. The group used a fake identity, Mia Clark, to manage the Social Research Center, a puppet think tank that recruited unwitting Latin American staff to spread anti-Ukraine propaganda. Analyst Lukasz Olejnik has since challenged the company's impact rating, arguing the operation primarily circulated within existing pro-Kremlin bubbles rather than infiltrating mainstream public debate.

selectedTweets.text: I must point out that OpenAI appears to oversell it. This is not Category 5 even in their own framework. The “Polish media” that picked up the Peru fake was essentially the pro-Russian weekly and one local portal. No evidence of mainstream reporting. The article was written by a guy who is on trial for spying for Russia, and the MEP it quoted is his political ally, who gave the comment when he asked for it. Looks less like a Russian fake breaking out into public debate and more like it circulating inside a pro-Kremlin bubble that was already receptive.
